verdict.rationale: The evidence documents an interactive terminal CLI (`kimi`) that starts a chat session and uses an interactive `/login` command, plus ACP connectivity for editors. Nothing documents a non-interactive, headless, or CI execution mode, such as a print/exec flag, scripted invocation, or CI setup guidance. The OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible Kimi API and API keys are developer building blocks on a separately positioned platform, not a headless mode of the product itself, so they earn no credit here.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation
